```{r}
#| label: Mediation analysis 

#renaming variables

    L01 = padre_vive_2010,
    L02 = madre_vive_2010,
    L03 = madre_estado_civil_2010, 
    L04 = madre_ocupacion_2010,
    L05 = madre_nivel_educ_2010,
    L06 = etnia, 
    L07 = region_2010,
    L11 = padre_vive_2013,
    L12 = madre_vive_2013,
    L13 = madre_estado_civil_2013,
    L14 = madre_ocupacion_2013,
    L15 = estrato_2013, 
    L16 = t_personas_2013,
    L21 = padre_vive_2016,
    L22 = madre_vive_2016,
    L23 = madre_estado_civil_2016,
    L24 = madre_ocupacion_2016, 
    L25 = estrato_2016,
    L26 = t_personas_2016, 
    X1 = estrato_2010,
    X2 = sexo, 
    X3 = edad_2010, 
    M1 = tot_insec_2010,
    M2 = tot_insec_2013,
    M3 = tot_insec_2016,
    Y = tot_dificultades_2016
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    starts_with("C0"),
    starts_with("L0"),
    starts_with("L1"),
    starts_with("L2"),
    X1, X2, X3, M1, M2, M3, Y
  ) %>% 
  mutate (ID= row_number(), 
          .before = 1)


#since we will be working with complete case analysis, we will transofrm NA's into "No info" category, to avoid as much data loss as possible  

vars <- c( "X2", "X3", "L01", "L02", "L03", "L04", "L05", "L06", "L07", "L11", "L12", "L13", "L14", "L15", "L16", "L21", "L22", "L23", "L24", "L25", "L26", "L27")

data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.factor),
      ~ droplevels(
        forcats::fct_na_value_to_level(.x, level = "No Info")
      )
    )
  )



#generating copy of observed exposure 
data$xstar <- data$X1

```

### Fitting mediator weights

```{r}
#regressions on mediators 
m1reg <- vglm (M1 ~ xstar + L01 +L02 + L03 + L04 + L05 +L06 + L07, 
               data = data, family = multinomial)

#without region
m2reg <- vglm (M2 ~ xstar + M1 + L01 +L02 + L03 + L04 + L05 +L06 + L07 + L11 + L12  + L14 + L15 +L16, 
               data = data, family = multinomial)



#without region at t2 and t3
m3reg <- vglm (M3 ~ xstar + M1 + M2 + L01 +L02 + L03 + L04 + L05 +L06 + L07 + L11 + L12 + L14 + L15  + L16 + L21 + L22 + L24 + L25 + L26  , 
               data = data, family = multinomial)

```

#### Assesing mediator model fit

We will proceed to check the accuracy of the mediator models at predicting the observed value by:

1.  obtaining the estimated probabilities for all categories of Neighborhood Perceived Insecurity estimated by the models
2.  Adding the observed value to the dataframe obtained in the previous step
3.  Creating a long version to observe level of neighborhood insecurity x actually observed value
4.  Identifying the probability of the observed value
5.  Plotting of the probabilities.

```{r}

# Predicted probabilities
exp.1 <- predict(m1reg, type = "response")

exp.2 <- predict(m2reg, type = "response")

exp.3 <- predict(m3reg, type = "response")


df.exp.1 <- as.data.frame (exp.1)

df.exp.2 <- as.data.frame (exp.2)

df.exp.3 <- as.data.frame (exp.3)

#adding observed value into dataframe of exp
df.exp.1$observed <- data$M1

df.exp.2$observed <- data$M2

df.exp.3$observed <- data$M3


#format long
exp.1.long <- df.exp.1 %>%
pivot_longer(
  cols = c(Low, Medium, High),
  names_to = "Category",
  values_to = "Predicted"
)


exp.2.long <- df.exp.2 %>%
pivot_longer(
  cols = c(Low, Medium, High),
  names_to = "Category",
  values_to = "Predicted"
)


exp.3.long <- df.exp.3 %>%
pivot_longer(
  cols = c(Low, Medium, High),
  names_to = "Category",
  values_to = "Predicted"
)

#if observed =1 if not =0 
exp.1.long <- exp.1.long %>%
mutate(
  Actual = ifelse(observed == Category, 1, 0)
)

exp.2.long <- exp.2.long %>%
mutate(
  Actual = ifelse(observed == Category, 1, 0)
)

exp.3.long <- exp.3.long %>%
mutate(
  Actual = ifelse(observed == Category, 1, 0)
)




```


Evaluating abnormal results for m2reg. Identifying that only one person has Pr \<0.01 in the actually observed value, therefore, not problematic.

```{r}

# Minimum probability for each category
apply(exp.2, 2, min)

# Number of probabilities below 0.01
colSums(exp.2 < 0.01)
obs.2 <- factor(obs.2, levels = colnames(exp.2))

# Probability of the observed category
p_obs.2 <- exp.2[
  cbind(seq_along(obs.2), as.integer(obs.2))
]

# Summary
summary(p_obs.2)

# Number of observed probabilities below 0.01
sum(p_obs.2 < 0.01)

# Minimum observed probability
min(p_obs.2)
```

#### Mediator weights

```{r}
#denominator weights 
m1dr <- as.matrix (predict (m1reg, type="response", newdata=data)) [cbind (1:nrow(data), data$M1)]
m2dr <- as.matrix (predict (m2reg, type="response", newdata=data)) [cbind (1:nrow(data), data$M2)]
m3dr <- as.matrix (predict (m3reg, type="response", newdata=data)) [cbind (1:nrow(data), data$M3)]


#numerator weights following counterfactual logic 
dattemp <- data 

dattemp <- dattemp[
  rep(seq_len(nrow(dattemp)), each = 2),
] %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  mutate(
    xstar = setdiff(c("Low-low", "Low", "Medium-Low"), as.character(first(X1)))
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

dattemp$xstar <- factor(dattemp$xstar, levels = levels(dattemp$X1))


#regression on mediators for counterfactuals to obtain numerator 

m1nr <- as.matrix (predict (m1reg, type="response", newdata=dattemp)) [cbind(1:nrow(dattemp), rep(dattemp$M1,))]
m2nr <- as.matrix (predict (m2reg, type="response", newdata=dattemp)) [cbind(1:nrow(dattemp), rep(dattemp$M2,))]
m3nr <- as.matrix (predict (m3reg, type="response", newdata=dattemp)) [cbind(1:nrow(dattemp), rep(dattemp$M3,))]

#calculating mediator weights 

dattemp$wmed1 <- m1nr / rep(m1dr, each = 2)
dattemp$wmed2 <- m2nr / rep(m2dr, each = 2)
dattemp$wmed3 <- m3nr / rep(m3dr, each = 2)

#adding weights of 1 to original dataset since a = a*
data <- data %>% 
  mutate (wmed1 = 1,
          wmed2 = 1, 
          wmed3 = 1)
```

#### Fitting model for exposure

```{r}
#fitting exposure model to obtain weight of exposure 
Xreg <- vglm (X1 ~ L01 +L02 + L03 + L04 + L05 +L06 + L07, data= data, family = multinomial, refLevel = "1")

Xprob <- as.matrix(predict (Xreg, type = "response")) #probability of exposure value being actually observed

colX_index <- match(
  as.character(data$X1),
  colnames(Xprob)
)



#identifying the probability of the actually observed value given covariates
Xprob_observed <- Xprob[
  cbind(seq_len(nrow(data)), colX_index)
]


#calculating the weights based on Xp_observed
Xweight_prob <- 1/Xprob_observed



#attaching weight to ID
Xweights_data <- data %>%
  mutate(Xweight_prob=Xweight_prob) %>%
  dplyr::select(ID, Xweight_prob)




#adding weight variable into original dataset
data <- data %>% left_join(Xweights_data, by="ID")
dattemp <- dattemp %>% left_join(Xweights_data, by="ID")


#binding datasets 
fulldata <- rbind (data, dattemp)
fulldata <- fulldata[order(fulldata$ID),]

#generating cumulative weight and full weight variables since we're interested in the end of study outcome

fulldata <- fulldata %>%
  mutate(
    weight_med = wmed1*wmed2*wmed3, 
    W = weight_med*Xweight_prob)
```

### Model fitting

```{r}
#| label: outcomes mediation

fit_out1 <- geeglm(Y~X1+xstar,data=fulldata,corstr="independence",
                   family="gaussian", weights=W,id=fulldata$ID,scale.fix=TRUE)


#model outcome
tidy_fit <- tidy(fit_out1, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)
tidy_fit
write.csv(tidy_fit,"outcome.csv")


anov.fit <- anova (fit_out1)
anov.fit
write.csv(anov.fit,"Anova.csv")


plotEst(fit_out1)




```

### Weight assessment

```{r}
#| label: Checking weights

#graphical assessment
#assessing weights graphically to see from where the high values come from


#distribution of exposure weights
hist(
  data$Xweight_prob, #after running this we can observe that its the X weights
  breaks = 30,
  main = "Distribution of IPW in x",
  xlab = "Weights"
)




#distribution of IPW
hist_w <- ggplot(fulldata, aes(x = W, fill = ..count..)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, color = "black", alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "C", direction = -1) +
  labs(title = "Histogram of IPW Weights", x = "IPW Weight", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~X1)



#Boxplot of IPW Weights to visually detect outliers
boxplot_IPWoutliers <- ggplot(fulldata, aes(x= X1, y = W, fill= X1)) +
  geom_boxplot(color = "black", outlier.colour = "#1B4F72") +
  labs(title = "Boxplot of IPW Weights", x= "SES", y = "IPW Weight") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16)

weights <- grid.arrange(hist_w, boxplot_IPWoutliers, ncol = 2)

ggsave("hist_w.png", hist_w, width=20, height=10)
ggsave("boxplot_IPWoutliers.png", boxplot_IPWoutliers, width=15, height=10)

```

```{r}
#taking a further look into the weights 
summary (fulldata$W)
quantile(fulldata$W, probs = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.95, 0.99)) 

#calculating ratio maximum:mean
ipw_ratio <- max(fulldata$W) / mean(fulldata$W) #13.8
ipw_ratio

sum(fulldata$W > 10, na.rm = TRUE)
sum(fulldata$W > 20, na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: checking SMD of baseline confounders on the exposure

cov.bal_data <- fulldata %>%
  distinct(ID, .keep_all = TRUE)


cov.bal <- bal.tab(
  X1 ~ L01 +L02 + L03 + L04 + L05 +L06 + L07,
  data = cov.bal_data,
  weights = "Xweight_prob",
  un = TRUE,
  pairwise = TRUE,
  binary = "raw"
)


print(cov.bal)

```

## Sensitivity analysis

```{r}
abn_weights <- fulldata %>%
  filter(Xweight_prob > 10) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    ID, X1, L01, L02, L03 , L04 , L05 ,L06 , L07,
    W
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(W))

abn_weights
```

```{r}
#| label: Identification of problematic cases within sample for truncation



fulldata <- fulldata %>%
  mutate(
    W_95 = pmin(W, quantile(W, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE))
  )


fulldata

summary (fulldata$W_95)
```

#### Refitting of model 

```{r}
#| label: Refitting model with truncated data 

fit_out.w95 <- geeglm(Y~X1+xstar,data=fulldata,corstr="independence",
                  family="gaussian", weights=W_95,id=fulldata$ID,scale.fix=TRUE)

summary (fit_out.w95)

tidy_fit.95 <- tidy(fit_out.w95, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)

write.csv(tidy_fit.95,"trunc_outcome.csv")

plotEst(fit_out.w95)

anov.fit95 <- anova (fit_out.w95)
write.csv(anov.fit95,"Anova_trunc.csv")
```
